# R313 — Corrected measured prefill ledger and next-axis ranking

Date: 2026-10-13
Scope: read-only review of closed B570 evidence, curated prefill source, and XeStrata b9 Level Zero copy-queue source. No builds, runs, GPU/model access, process inspection, or cleanup were performed.

## Correction to R312

R312's characterization of the result as source-only was inaccurate. The closed production-leaf profile is an actual instrumented Arc B570 run, not a source estimate. Its report and model-result record establish a valid 32K prompt plus 16 generated tokens, all 129,820 selected events completed, exact output IDs and LP5, and clean normal quit/fault status. This is valid diagnostic evidence; the run is explicitly not speed-eligible. The event totals therefore describe observed selected-command spans, not a quiet wall-time speedup or a critical-path decomposition.

The closed profile reports 97,732 host-USM→device-USM copy commands and 200,326,113,280 requested bytes, with 69.651 s summed action spans and 11.092 s summed host-submit time. It also reports 5,944 grouped XMX GU calls (3.345 s summed service spans; 0.681 s host submit), 5,944 grouped XMX Down calls (1.662 s; 0.628 s), 10,096 native-dequant GU calls (2.545 s; 1.096 s), and 10,096 native-dequant Down calls (1.961 s; 1.094 s). These sums may overlap in time; they are not PCIe bandwidth, physical bytes, additive wall time, or fractions of the critical path. Dense/GDN/QSA work was not captured. Instrumented prefill time was 105,936.4 ms; do not compare it directly with the separate quiet performance summary.

The separate same-binary calibration has four OFF/ON samples and a pooled +0.603% prefill delta; paired differences span -1,916.9 to +2,991.3 ms with opposite signs. It does not establish instrumentation neutrality or a speed effect. The event profile remains useful for command inventory and observed spans, not for ranking kernel-vs-copy critical-path share.

A separate closed B570 decode-critical-path report gives the relevant quiet A/B: on the same 32K+16 setup, native dequant batching reduced kernel count from 187,050 to 20,192, while H2D requests remained 97,728 and logical bytes 199,990,579,200. Three clean samples per side measured prefill 359.02→376.42 tokens/s (4.66% lower prefill time); decode moved 8.10→8.27 tokens/s and was not attributed to this prefill change. IDs/LP5 and health/quit checks passed. Thus a meaningful prefill improvement was already measured without reducing copy requests. The new leaf-event totals agree with that request count to within 4 calls; they must not be treated as a new performance A/B.

## Candidate comparison

**16K prompt chunks:** Source history estimates about 1.67 GiB additional peak demand at 16K over the current 8K chunk. The 16K shared region is GDN-dominated (2,444 MiB versus a 2,049 MiB QSA region in the earlier source estimate). Phase aliasing embedding/bo/PLE-embedding storage was estimated to save 320 MiB at 16K; reducing GDN tile residency toward the QSA floor was estimated to save another 395 MiB, but changes recurrence/convolution-state liveness and needs numerical validation. These are source-derived estimates, not measured allocator high-water or proof of fit. The current closed run does not report sufficient free-memory headroom to authorize a 16K run. A four-to-two chunk reduction could reduce repeated per-chunk expert transfers, but that count reduction and any wall-time benefit remain projections until measured. This has the higher potential to reduce work, with substantial capacity/liveness and correctness risk.

**Xe b9 copy-only queue:** Curated source currently uses a generic in-order SYCL copy queue (prefill.cpp, .copy = stream_create(), source SHA prefix ececd50d). Host-stager reuse waits for each slot's prior dma_done; each copy_async_after depends on the slot's used event and records completion; issued_one publishes the event only after recording it on the copy queue. Reader credits and queue drains remain part of teardown. The Xe b9 implementation selects a Level Zero queue group having COPY but no COMPUTE, creates an in-order asynchronous immediate command list, imports it as a SYCL queue with ownership transfer, and falls back to a generic stream if loader/API discovery or a copy-only queue is unavailable. The Xe prefill path selects that stream but retains the event/lifetime protocol. It changes queue assignment, not the number of copies or bytes.

The Xe source comment records a B70 32K observation of 2,312 versus 2,305 tokens/s with the copy engine (about -0.30%) and says copies were already behind kernels. Treat this as a source comment, not a retained replicated benchmark receipt or proof for the present curated build. It lowers expected payoff but does not establish no effect on this exact image/driver. The native Level Zero interop also adds compatibility surface: Intel's SYCL backend extension documents make_queue from an immediate command list, ownership transfer, and the requirement that command lists be in-order for the L0 v2 adapter. It does not guarantee that a B570 exposes a copy-only group or that the driver schedules the work independently.

## Rank and safe next measurement

Rank first a **bounded copy-queue A/B**, not a 16K execution. This is the safest measurable single performance axis: it does not increase model memory, does not alter tensor arithmetic or copy count, and keeps the established slot/event lifetime protocol. Its expected gain is low given the Xe source comment and the qualified native-dequant result, but an exact-build A/B can resolve the question cheaply. Port only the queue-selection mechanism behind an explicit OFF/ON switch; first verify the copy-only group is actually selected (otherwise mark the arm fallback/ineligible). Run the same 32K+16 prompt, binary, device, and memory settings, with clean repeated OFF/ON quiet wall-time samples, exact IDs/LP5, health, safe quit, and event completeness. Preserve per-arm samples. Retain the port only if a repeatable wall-time improvement exceeds observed run-to-run noise and correctness is unchanged. Do not claim success from summed event-span reductions alone.

Keep 16K as the higher-upside second-stage work item, gated on an explicit peak-memory admission measurement with at least the project's required 512 MiB reserve after model load and all concurrent buffers are live. Measure the candidate aliasing/liveness changes separately and preserve a rollback point; then validate exact outputs and fault/quit handling before any 16K throughput claim. If the headroom gate fails, do not launch 16K. Do not stack the copy-queue change with 16K in one A/B.

## Primary Intel references

- Intel SYCL Level Zero backend extension: https://github.com/intel/llvm/blob/sycl/sycl/doc/extensions/supported/sycl_ext_oneapi_backend_level_zero.md — native queue/list import, ownership, immediate-list behavior, and in-order requirement.
- Intel Level Zero Immediate Command Lists guide: https://www.intel.com/content/www/us/en/developer/articles/guide/level-zero-immediate-command-lists.html — distinction between regular and immediate submission modes.
- Intel multi-Arc platform evaluation guide: https://cdrdv2-public.intel.com/863931/863931_Platform%20Evaluation%20Guide%20for%20Multi-ARC%20Solution_Rev1p0.pdf — reports queue-group Compute/Copy capabilities as device/platform-dependent; does not establish the B570 runtime group on this setup.

These references explain API and capability concepts; they are not performance evidence for the tested B570.
